name: Laboratory condenser
definition: Jacketed glass tube through which coolant flows to turn vapour back into liquid in distillation or reflux.

name: Laboratory autoclave
definition: Pressure chamber that sterilises laboratory ware, media and waste with steam.

name: Laboratory shaker
definition: Device that mixes samples in vessels by orbital, reciprocating or rocking motion.

name: Rotary evaporator
definition: Device that removes solvent from a sample by rotating a flask in a heated bath under reduced pressure.

name: Laminar-flow cabinet (clean bench)
definition: Cabinet that blows HEPA-filtered air over the work surface to keep samples free of contamination.

name: Biosafety cabinet
definition: HEPA-filtered enclosed cabinet that protects the user, the sample and the room when handling biological material.

name: Electron microscope
definition: Microscope that forms an image with a beam of electrons instead of light (scanning or transmission; tabletop models included).

name: Scanning probe microscope
definition: Microscope that maps a surface by scanning it with a fine physical probe (atomic force, scanning tunnelling).

name: Spectrometer
definition: Instrument that splits light from a sample into a spectrum and measures it (UV-Vis, infrared, Raman, emission); a hand spectroscope is this kind.

name: Mass spectrometer
definition: Instrument that ionises a sample and sorts the ions by mass to charge to identify its components.

name: Chromatograph
definition: Instrument that separates the components of a sample by passing it through a column (gas or liquid chromatography, HPLC).

name: Elemental analyser
definition: Instrument that measures the elements (carbon, hydrogen, nitrogen, sulphur and others) a sample contains, usually by combustion.

name: Glove box
definition: Sealed cabinet with fitted gloves for working on samples in an inert or isolated atmosphere.

name: Climatic chamber
definition: Cabinet that holds samples at a set temperature and humidity, below or above room temperature, for stability or ageing tests.

name: Laboratory stirrer
definition: Device that mixes a liquid sample with a stirring bar or paddle, magnetic or overhead, often with a heating plate.

name: Laboratory water bath
definition: Heated tank of water that holds sample vessels at a set temperature.

name: Laboratory circulator (thermostat)
definition: Unit that heats or cools a liquid and pumps it to hold a bath or connected apparatus at a set temperature.

name: Viscometer
definition: Instrument that measures the viscosity of a liquid sample.

name: Rheometer
definition: Instrument that measures how a sample flows and deforms under applied stress or strain.

name: Microplate reader
definition: Instrument that measures absorbance, fluorescence or luminescence of samples in the wells of a microplate.

name: Laboratory thermometer
definition: Thermometer made to read the temperature of a sample, liquid-in-glass or digital probe.

name: Cloud sensor
definition: Instrument that detects cloud cover by measuring the infrared temperature of the sky.

name: Sky-quality meter
definition: Instrument that measures the brightness of the night sky.

name: Microscope stage
definition: Stage made to fit a microscope, manual or motorised, that holds and moves the specimen.

name: Dew shield
definition: Tube fitted to the front of a telescope to keep dew and stray light off the objective.

name: Telescope focuser
definition: Draw-tube unit fitted to a telescope that moves the eyepiece or camera to focus (Crayford, rack and pinion, motorised).

name: Molecular model kit
definition: Set of atom and bond pieces for building models of molecules, made to teach chemistry.

name: Schmidt astrograph (Schmidt camera)
definition: Catadioptric imaging telescope with a full-aperture Schmidt corrector and a spherical primary that forms the image on a camera at prime focus inside the tube, with no eyepiece position.

name: Telescope finder
definition: Small sighting device fitted on a telescope tube to aim it: optical finderscope, right-angle finder, red-dot or ring sight; the polar scope is C6.5.1.09.

name: Barlow lens
definition: Negative lens unit fitted in a telescope's eyepiece barrel that multiplies the effective focal length, and so the magnification, by a stated factor.

name: Astronomical filter
definition: Filter threaded or mounted for a telescope eyepiece barrel, filter wheel or camera train that passes chosen wavelengths (colour, moon, light-pollution, nebula, narrowband); solar filters are C6.5.1.04

name: Microscope objective
definition: Objective lens made to screw into a microscope nosepiece (RMS or M25 thread), sold apart from the stand; objective class and tube-length standard are attributes.

name: Microscope eyepiece (ocular)
definition: Eyepiece made for a microscope tube (23.2 or 30 mm and other barrels), sold apart from the stand; WF or SWF field and power are attributes.
